population.citation: HYDE 3.3 (2023), Gapminder Population v7 (2022), and United Nations DESA, Population Division, World Population Prospects 2024, with processing by Our World in Data.

gdp.citation: Bolt, Jutta and Jan Luiten van Zanden (2024). Maddison style estimates of the evolution of the world economy: A new 2023 update. Journal of Economic Surveys. MPD 2023 via Our World in Data.

arable.citation: FAO electronic files and website, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, via World Development Indicators, AG.LND.ARBL.ZS.

cropland.citation: Klein Goldewijk, K., Beusen, A., Doelman, J., and Stehfest, E. (2017, database updated 2024). Anthropogenic land use estimates for the Holocene. HYDE 3.3 baseline global aggregates via DataHub.

croplandRegional.citation: Klein Goldewijk, K., Beusen, A., Doelman, J., and Stehfest, E. (2017). Anthropogenic land use estimates for the Holocene – HYDE 3.2. Earth System Science Data 9, 927–953, Table 2. Regional estimates converted from million hectares to square kilometres.

census.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Historical Population Change Data (1910–2020), Resident Population rows for United States and Puerto Rico.

lifeExpectancy.citation: Period life expectancy at birth. Riley (2005); Zijdeman et al. (2015); Human Mortality Database (2025); UN World Population Prospects (2024), compiled by Our World in Data.
lifeExpectancy.note: Long-run country and regional series from 1543; the world aggregate starts in 1770. Period life expectancy summarizes age-specific death rates in a single year and can dip during crises.

literacy.citation: Adult literacy rate, UNESCO Institute for Statistics (2026), compiled by Our World in Data.
literacy.note: Adult literacy is survey-based and reported at irregular intervals; later surveys replace or revise earlier estimates. A 100% value reflects the reported rate, not universal measurement.

pasture.citation: Klein Goldewijk, K., Beusen, A., Doelman, J., and Stehfest, E. (2017, database updated 2024). Anthropogenic land use estimates for the Holocene. HYDE 3.3 baseline global aggregates via DataHub. Includes the pasture aggregate.

density.citation: Population density per km² of land area. HYDE (2023); Gapminder (2022); UN World Population Prospects (2024); UN FAO (2024), compiled by Our World in Data.
density.note: Gridded historical reconstruction aggregated to present-day boundaries; projected years after 2023 are excluded.
licenses: HYDE / Gapminder / UN / OWID · CC BY 4.0

worldGdp.citation: World GDP in constant international-$. Eurostat, OECD, IMF and World Bank (2026); Bolt and van Zanden – Maddison Project Database 2023; Maddison Database 2010, via Our World in Data.
worldGdp.note: Sparse historical benchmarks with annual modern observations; gaps are not interpolated.
licenses: Maddison / World Bank / OWID · CC BY 4.0

urbanShare.citation: Share of population living in urban areas. United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2025), via Our World in Data.
urbanShare.note: Urban share by present-day boundaries; years after 2023 are excluded from the historical series.
licenses: UN DESA / OWID · CC BY 3.0 IGO
